description:
The `gf2-sim` README is the crate's concise adopter-facing entry page: what the crate provides, when to choose it, and where its reference material lives.

## Background

Permanent pages target researchers evaluating or adopting gf2 and assume technical competence. Explanatory prose is freshly authored; only independently verified code, commands, equations, identifiers and empirical data are reused from prior material. Pages state current supported behavior only. A crate README is the crate's entry page; the docs index links it.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `crates/gf2-sim/README.md` states the crate's purpose and when to choose it, verified against the crate's current public API and Cargo manifest, and links to the pages that own its capabilities and feature flags. It carries no capability list.
- [hard] REQ-02: Its prose and structure are freshly authored; reused items from gf2-sim crate and module Rustdoc are limited to verified code, commands and identifiers.
- [hard] REQ-03: It carries no performance figures, API walkthrough duplicating Rustdoc, hand-maintained example list, history, or future promises; it links to `docs/index.md` and to the crate's Rustdoc through the locally generated `target/doc/gf2_sim/index.html` path, next to the command that builds it.
- [hard] REQ-04: It links to no file under a crate-local `docs/` directory.
- [hard] REQ-05: Its links and commands resolve.
- [hard] REQ-06: The crate section of `docs/index.md` links `crates/gf2-sim/README.md`.

## Decisions

- DEC-01: The owner decided on 2026-10-03 that a crate README states purpose and links only, that the locally generated Rustdoc link satisfies REQ-03, and that a documentation-only issue carries no Rust CI criterion.
title: Write the gf2-sim README as its entry page
